ai.title: infisical-run executor loads TS directly
ai.summary: Switched `@codebuff/build-tools:infisical-run` implementation from `./dist/executors/infisical-run/executor.js` to `./executors/infisical-run/executor.ts`. Removed `dependsOn: ["@codebuff/build-tools:build"]` from the `evals` project target to eliminate build dependency for eval execution. This change affects `build-tools/executors.json` and `evals/project.json`. The executor now relies on runtime TypeScript compilation rather than pre-built artifacts.

eli5.text: When you run an automated test or evaluation using the internal tooling, it now loads the instructions directly from the source file instead of waiting for a separate pre-compilation step to finish first. This removes a build prerequisite that previously had to complete before these runs could start, so the workflow can kick off sooner without that extra prerequisite. The change is internal and already live, affecting only the company's internal evaluation runs, it's a behind-the-scenes tweak to cut down on overhead, with no new user-facing behavior.

ai.title: Remove explicit build-tools dependency from infisical-run targets
ai.summary: Reverts the addition of `dependsOn: ["@codebuff/build-tools:build"]` to all `infisical-run` executor targets across backend, common, evals, npm-app, billing, and web projects. The explicit dependency was removed from `project.json` files, likely resolving build graph issues or redundancy introduced in a previous fix. This change affects the Nx build orchestration for these specific targets.

eli5.text: When certain developer tools run, like starting the backend, doing database work, running evaluations, building the npm package, handling billing tests, or running web tasks, they no longer wait for a shared helper project to finish building first. This only affects developers running these tools locally, since the shared build helper now loads what it needs on demand instead of requiring a separate build step. If you looked, you'd see fewer dependency wires between project config files, and builds that kick off a little faster because they skip waiting on that extra step. The change is already live.

ai.title: Move build-tools into packages workspace
ai.summary: Relocated build-tools directory to packages/build-tools. Updated root package.json workspaces array to remove explicit build-tools entry, relying on packages/* glob. Adjusted project.json cwd fields and tsconfig.json extends path to reflect new location.

eli5.text: The team moved the collection of build tools into a shared folder alongside other project packages, so all projects are now organized in one consistent location. If you looked at the project's configuration, you would see the build tools living under that shared packages area instead of being listed separately. Anyone working on this project would now find the tools grouped together with everything else, rather than tucked away in their own standalone spot.

ai.title: codebuff npm package bumped to 1.0.326
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.326 in npm-app/package.json. Includes newline fix at end of file. Affects codebuff npm package.

eli5.text: The CodeWhisperer assistant (the thing the codebuff package powers) stopped showing a weird blank line at the very end of files when it made edits. If you've ever noticed an extra empty row appearing after your last line of code when the assistant changed something, that glitch is gone now. This is a tiny behind-the-scenes packaging update, just making sure the installed tool stays current.

ai.title: Terminal PTY logging captures full output
ai.summary: runSinglePtyCommand now returns fullOutput alongside filteredOutput in npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts. runCommandPty accumulates full output from cd, command, exit-code, and cwd probes into fullCombinedOutput. logger.error calls include fullExitCodeOutput or fullCombinedOutput when needle matches fail.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the system now keeps a complete log of everything that was printed, including prompts and text that gets filtered out during normal operation. This means that if something goes wrong, like not being able to detect the exit status of a command or determine the current directory, the error messages logged internally will contain the full output, giving developers more context to understand why a command failed. Only developers working on the terminal functionality will notice this change; it is an internal improvement that makes debugging terminal sessions easier but does not change what you see or how the system behaves.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.327
ai.summary: Package version in `npm-app/package.json` incremented from 1.0.326 to 1.0.327. This is a routine release marker for the `codebuff` npm package. No functional code changes included in this commit.

eli5.text: The version label for the AI assistant software was bumped from one release number to the next on June 14, 2025. This is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping update that marks a new version being shipped; it doesn't add visible features or change behavior you would notice. The version bump bundles one user-facing improvement: terminal command logs now capture full output instead of only the filtered portion, so logs record everything rather than a trimmed view. This update is live today and applies to anyone using the assistant's terminal command handling. No other user-facing changes are included in this release.

ai.title: Git evals clone guard and error logging
ai.summary: Added post-clone validation in setup-test-repo.ts to throw if .git directory missing. Updated run-git-evals.ts to log specific error context before rejection. Scope limited to evals/git-evals subsystem. Prevents silent failures during test repo setup.

eli5.text: When the test environment sets up a trial project, it now checks that the project was actually copied correctly before moving on. If the copy failed, the process stops and records what went wrong, rather than silently continuing. If you were watching the logs, you'd now see a clearer error tied to the specific failed copy and repository. This only affects internal testing of repository tools.

ai.title: Improve git test repo setup auth and validation
ai.summary: The `setupTestRepo` function in `evals/git-evals/setup-test-repo.ts` was rewritten to use `execFileSync` instead of `execSync` for safer command execution and added robust authentication handling for GitHub private repositories via `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`. This change ensures test repos clone correctly in CI environments (GitHub Actions, Render) by converting SSH URLs to authenticated HTTPS and disabling interactive prompts. The function now includes explicit verification steps, checking for `.git` existence, `git status`, and commit history count, with detailed error logging and troubleshooting guidance for authentication failures.

eli5.text: When you or someone on your team runs an internal automated test that downloads a sample code project from GitHub to check that things still work, that download will now succeed reliably in shared, password-free environments (like the company's scheduled check systems) by logging in automatically with a stored GitHub credential. The system now also double-checks the download actually completed and gives a clearer message if the login credential is missing or wrong, instead of just failing silently.

ai.title: Improve AI SDK error reporting in stream handler
ai.summary: Error handling in `promptAiSdkStream` now preserves the original error object by setting it as the `cause` when the error is an `Error` instance. Non-Error payloads are stringified with a consistent `Error from AI SDK:` prefix. This change applies to `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` and affects non-production environments only.

eli5.text: When the AI system hits an error while generating a response, it now includes the original error details so developers can see exactly what went wrong, instead of just a generic message. Non-error responses are still shown with a clear 'AI system error:' label for consistency. This only applies to testing and development environments, not the live production system.

ai.title: Spinner text customization
ai.summary: Spinner class accepts custom text via start() method. Default 'Thinking' replaced with context-specific labels like 'Restoring', 'Saving', 'Storing API Key', 'Using browser'. Updates applied across checkpoint handlers, CLI, client, and tool handlers. Removed unused log() method from Spinner.

eli5.text: When the app shows its spinning progress indicator while it's working, it now shows a label that explains what it's actually doing, like "Restoring", "Saving", "Storing API Key", or "Using browser", instead of always just "Thinking". You'd notice this because the text next to the spinner animates to match the real task in progress, and the developers also cleaned up some old unused helper code from that spinner component while making this switch across the command-line tools, the client, and the browser-related helpers.

ai.title: Add Loading spinner to checkpoint save
ai.summary: Spinner label changed to 'Loading' during readyPromise wait in saveCheckpoint. Added 'Loading' spinner before awaiting readyPromise, moved 'Saving' spinner to start after waitForPreviousCheckpoint. Affects npm-app/src/cli-handlers/checkpoint.ts.

eli5.text: When you trigger a save of your work, the screen now shows a message that says 'Loading' first, then switches to 'Saving' once that initial step is done. You might notice the two-stage feedback briefly as the system prepares before actually writing the save. This is live today for anyone using the app's save feature.

ai.title: Tool renderers support callback return
ai.summary: ToolCallRenderer interface updated to allow onToolStart, onParamStart, onParamChunk, onParamEnd, and onToolEnd to return void callbacks alongside string outputs. XML stream parser logic modified to execute returned functions when output is not a string. Affects npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts and npm-app/src/utils/xml-stream-parser.ts. Enables side-effect execution from renderer hooks without pushing to stream.

eli5.text: When the assistant works with tools during a conversation, certain helper functions can now choose to return a small action to run immediately instead of only returning text to display. The text you see in the stream is handled the same way as before, but these helpers can now also trigger side effects right away without adding anything to the visible output. This lets the interface do extra work behind the scenes at the exact moment a tool or parameter starts, updates, or finishes. The change is live in the application's internal rendering code today.

ai.title: Add Researching spinner, trim stream close tags
ai.summary: Replaced static 'Researching...' text with active Spinner component in tool-renderers.ts. Added trailing newlines to prompt lists. Removed trailing newline from auto-closed XML tags in xml-stream-parser.ts. Scope: npm-app UI, backend parser.

eli5.text: When the assistant is working through a multi-step task, you now see a spinning animation instead of a static message. Behind the scenes, the spinner replaces a plain text line in the tool-display code and adds consistent spacing around lists of prompts. The change affects only the visual feedback you see during tool use and is live today.

ai.title: getGitChanges returns empty on missing git binary
ai.summary: getGitChanges in npm-app/src/project-files.ts checks gitCommandIsAvailable() and returns empty strings for status, diff, diffCached, and lastCommitMessages when git is absent. Added explicit Promise return type to getGitChanges. Imported gitCommandIsAvailable from ./utils/git. Prevents execAsync failures on systems without git.

eli5.text: If the assistant tries to look at your project's version history (the Git record of your changes) on a machine where Git isn't installed, it will now quietly report that there's nothing to show instead of potentially crashing or spewing out error messages. The assistant was already designed to check whether Git exists on your system before it tries to run Git commands; this just makes sure that check is in place and that the function returns a clear, empty result when Git is missing, rather than letting the process fail mid-command. It's the kind of behind-the-scenes fix you'd notice only if you were running the app in an environment without Git and previously saw errors related to version-control features.

ai.title: maxIterations caps loopMainPrompt and research agent loops
ai.summary: Added maxIterations parameter to loopMainPrompt with DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 20, breaking the agent loop once iterations hit the cap. research.ts passes maxIterations = 10 into loopMainPrompt, replacing the previous agentStepsRemaining: 10 assignment. Backend only: loop-main-prompt.ts, research.ts. AgentStepsRemaining in AgentState still governs per-prompt step budget; maxIterations bounds the outer tool-call loop.

eli5.text: The agent now stops itself after a set number of steps instead of looping forever when it's researching or working through tasks. When running research tasks, it caps itself at 10 iterations, and in general use it will give up after 20 attempts, preventing infinite loops. If you were watching a task take unusually long, you'll now see it finish (or give up) with a clear endpoint, even if it hasn't fully completed the requested work.

ai.title: Catch research errors, log, cap prompts
ai.summary: Wrapped research execution in try/catch block within main-prompt.ts. Errors return formatted string instead of throwing. Added logger.debug for successful runs. research.ts now caps prompts at maxPrompts=10 via slice.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs out of its allowed number of research calls, it now stops cleanly and tells you something went wrong, instead of possibly continuing and getting overwhelmed. It also remembers a short note (the prompt and the result) for each research attempt, and logs it quietly for anyone checking the system later. This is live today and affects anyone whose assistant runs this research process.

ai.title: Update xml-stream-parser test expectations
ai.summary: Adjusts test assertions in xml-stream-parser.test.ts to remove trailing newlines from expected closing tags. Aligns expectations with current stream processing behavior. Internal test fix only.

eli5.text: If you opened the app today and watched the log inspector window, XML tag lines such as </param> and </test> would appear without an extra blank line after each one, because the test that confirms that formatting was corrected to match the actual output. The live behavior itself is unchanged; only the internal check that guarantees it stays that way was fixed.

ai.title: Terminal startup scripts await before command execution
ai.summary: Terminal process initialization in `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts` now awaits shell startup scripts via a `setupPromise` before executing user commands. Previous implementation wrote init commands asynchronously, risking race conditions where commands executed before environment variables or aliases from sourced configs were available. The change refactors `shellInitCommands` from a single string to an array of commands, each wrapped with prompt identifier setup, and enforces sequential execution using `runSinglePtyCommand`. This ensures the persistent PTY is fully initialized before `runCommandPty` proceeds.

eli5.text: When you open a terminal window in the app, it used to rush ahead and run your commands before fully loading your custom settings, aliases, or environment variables, sometimes causing confusing errors or missing tools. Now, the terminal waits patiently for your startup scripts to finish (like your ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc) before letting you type or run anything. If you looked at the terminal opening, you'd see it pause briefly, ensuring everything from your config files is properly loaded before showing you the prompt. This change is live today, improving reliability for anyone using the terminal feature in the npm-app.
